fields.explanation: The T in GPT is Transformer: stacked self-attention layers where each position attends to the other positions in the context in one pass instead of waiting for a previous step, which is what makes training parallel over the sequence. fields.hint: Ask what each setting keeps when the top token already holds almost all the mass, and when the top twenty are nearly tied.
fields.explanation: Top-k always keeps k candidates, so on a flat distribution it cuts off reasonable tokens and on a peaked one it admits junk; top-p sizes the set to the distribution, keeping just enough tokens to reach mass p. Over logits [8, 1, 0.5, 0.2, 0.1] the nucleus at p=0.9 is a single token, while over [1, 0.9, 0.85, 0.8, 0.75] it is all five - top-k=3 keeps three in both cases. Neither is deterministic on its own: both still sample from whatever survives, and both work from the same ranked next-token probabilities, so where the softmax sits is not what separates them.
